headline: Iran's attacks on tankers near the Strait of Hormuz drove Brent more than 3 percent higher to about 104 dollars a barrel, which pushed the Nifty 50 to its lowest close in 52 weeks at 22,231.80 and kept the US 10 year Treasury yield above 5.2 percent, while a Financial Times report that OpenAI's annualised revenue is nearer 50 billion dollars than the 70 billion previously cited took 1.25 percent off the Nasdaq Composite.

summary.us: The Nasdaq Composite fell 1.25 percent to 27,193.34 and the S&P 500 lost 0.47 percent to 7,765.36, a second straight decline after records earlier in the week, while the Dow added 0.1 percent to 51,231.64 as money rotated out of chips and into energy. The trigger was a Financial Times report that OpenAI told investors its annualised revenue is approaching 50 billion dollars against the 68 to 70 billion previously reported, which sent Arm down 6.48 percent, Oracle 5.48 percent, Intel 5.34 percent and Micron 4.79 percent; the 10 year Treasury yield eased to 5.231 percent after touching its highest level since 2002, and weekly jobless claims came in at 197,000.
summary.india: The Nifty 50 fell 1.64 percent to 22,231.80, its lowest close in 52 weeks after an intraday low of 22,179.90, and the Bank Nifty lost 0.98 percent to 54,515.05, with Brent above 104 dollars and Wednesday's RBI repo rate hike to 5.50 percent setting the tone. Provisional exchange data put foreign institutional investors at about 12,944 crore rupees of net cash selling against roughly 10,703 crore rupees of domestic buying, Adani Enterprises fell 5.36 percent and ITC 4.03 percent on a reported block deal near 9,400 crore rupees, the rupee held at 96.78 per dollar on what traders described as central bank intervention, and TCS opened the results season with second quarter profit up about 15 percent at 13,934 crore rupees and a second interim dividend of 12 rupees a share.
summary.global: The Nikkei 225 closed 1.42 percent lower at 69,042.11 and the Hang Seng fell 1.43 percent to 23,785.79, while the KOSPI dropped 2.62 percent to 6,625.93 as Samsung Electronics' preliminary third quarter numbers left investors focused on a possible peak in memory prices and Samsung shares fell 2.42 percent. In Europe the DAX lost 1.18 percent and the FTSE 100 held up at a 0.16 percent decline as BP rose 4.16 percent on crude, and TSMC reported September revenue up 54.6 percent from a year earlier at about 511.9 billion New Taiwan dollars, taking third quarter revenue to roughly 1.49 trillion and above consensus, though its ADR still fell 3.01 percent in the US chip selloff.

calendar.what: Preliminary University of Michigan consumer sentiment, 10:00 am ET. Two Nasdaq IPOs are set to price, Retension Pharmaceuticals and TRex Bio

India September CPI, 5:30 pm IST. August was 4.82 percent year on year and Trading Economics forecasts 4.9 percent. HCLTech reports Q2 FY27 and considers a third interim dividend. Columbus Day in the US, bond market closed and stock markets open

US bank earnings open the third quarter season: JPMorgan Chase around 7:00 am ET with the call at 8:30 am ET, consensus about 5.90 to 5.94 dollars a share on roughly 51.2 billion dollars of revenue, alongside Wells Fargo, Citigroup and Goldman Sachs. Apple is reported to be unveiling a smart home hub, a new HomePod mini and an updated Apple TV 4K. HD Fire Protect IPO opens in India. Reserve Bank of Australia policy decision

US September CPI, 8:30 am ET, per the Bureau of Labor Statistics release schedule. Record date for the TCS second interim dividend of 12 rupees a share. Tata Technologies Q2 results. Bitari is expected to price on Nasdaq this week
US September PPI. Wipro declares Q2 FY27 results after market hours. HD Fire Protect IPO closes. TSMC and ASML third quarter reports are expected in this week, per Schwab's week ahead
Preorders open for the Apple iPhone Duo foldable at 1,999 dollars in the US, ahead of a 23 October release

Jio Platforms is reported to be opening its anchor book, with the issue reportedly running 21 to 23 October and listing on 28 October. The company has SEBI approval from 28 August 2026 but has not announced dates or a price band

weekly.narrative: The bond market set the terms for four days and then handed them back on Friday. The US 10 year Treasury yield touched about 5.23 percent intraday midweek, described in coverage as the highest since June 2007, which pushed the dollar index to fresh 2026 highs, sent gold about 3.5 percent lower on the week and left the Dow down 1.3 percent and the S and P 500 down 0.3 percent even after Friday's bounce. Friday's September payrolls print of 29,000 against about 90,000 expected, with unemployment at 4.2 percent, cut October Fed hike pricing to near 37 percent from roughly 70 percent earlier in the week, and the Nasdaq Composite rose 1.19 percent with Nvidia at an intraday record and Tesla up 4.65 percent on 486,532 third quarter deliveries. India had the worse week and the shorter one: the Nifty fell 2.78 percent to 22,421.95 by Thursday's close, within 0.4 percent of its 52 week low, on rate increase fears, 91 dollar crude and foreign selling of about 44,000 crore rupees in September, before markets shut on Friday for Gandhi Jayanti. Hong Kong reopened from its own holiday to its largest fall since March with HSBC down 5.7 percent, Tokyo slipped as September core CPI came in at 2.7 percent against 2.4 percent expected, and silver lost 5.5 percent while copper held near records on tight supply. Next week turns on the 7 October FOMC minutes and the Reserve Bank decision the same day, with TCS opening India's earnings season on 8 October and the Strait of Hormuz still the swing factor for oil.
